title: Choosing Between Bli-Passive and S-Passive
goal: Use modern Bokmål passive forms in present, modal, past, and perfect contexts.

objectives.statement: Use modern Bokmål passive forms in present, modal, past, and perfect contexts.

spans.value: Maya has applied for permission to build a small balcony. She calls the municipal planning office because the online system shows several different messages about her application.
Søknaden min står fortsatt som mottatt. Betyr det at ingen har sett på den?

blocks.translation: My application is still listed as received. Does that mean nobody has looked at it?

spans.value: Nei, alle søknader registreres automatisk når de kommer inn.

blocks.translation: No, all applications are registered automatically when they arrive.

spans.value: Hva skjer etterpå?

blocks.translation: What happens after that?

spans.value: Først blir søknaden kontrollert av en saksbehandler. Deretter vurderes tegningene.

blocks.translation: First, the application is checked by a case officer. Then the drawings are assessed.

spans.value: Jeg fikk en melding om at et vedlegg mangler.

blocks.translation: I received a message saying that an attachment is missing.

spans.value: Ja, vedlegget må sendes inn før saken kan behandles videre.

blocks.translation: Yes, the attachment must be submitted before the case can be processed further.

spans.value: Jeg sendte det inn i går kveld.

blocks.translation: I submitted it yesterday evening.

spans.value: Da har det kanskje ikke blitt registrert ennå. Systemet oppdateres bare om morgenen.

blocks.translation: Then it may not have been registered yet. The system is updated only in the morning.

spans.value: Hvor lang tid tar det vanligvis?

blocks.translation: How long does it usually take?

spans.value: De fleste søknader behandles innen tre uker. Din søknad ble mottatt for åtte dager siden, så den blir sannsynligvis avgjort neste uke.

blocks.translation: Most applications are processed within three weeks. Your application was received eight days ago, so it will probably be decided next week.

spans.value: Får jeg beskjed med en gang?

blocks.translation: Will I be notified immediately?

spans.value: Ja. Når saken har blitt avgjort, sendes vedtaket til deg digitalt.

blocks.translation: Yes. Once the case has been decided, the decision is sent to you digitally.

spans.value: The conversation contains two common ways of forming the passive in modern Bokmål:

en.value: All applications are registered automatically.
First, the application is checked.

spans.value: Both sentences focus on what happens to an application rather than on who performs the action. The choice between the two passive forms depends partly on time and partly on how the speaker presents the action.

sections.title: What the passive helps you say

spans.value: In an active sentence, the person or organization performing an action is normally the subject.

en.value: A case officer checks the application.

spans.value: In the passive voice (passiv), the affected person or thing becomes the subject.

no.value: Søknaden blir kontrollert av en saksbehandler.

en.value: The application is checked by a case officer.

spans.value: The passive is useful when the performer is unknown, obvious, unimportant, or less important than the procedure or result. Eirik is explaining what happens to Maya’s application, so he often leaves the municipal employees in the background.
Modern Bokmål commonly uses two passive constructions:

items.value: the bli-passive (bli-passiv), such as blir behandlet

spans.value: You already know the basic forms. This chapter concentrates on choosing and building them in present, modal, past, and perfect contexts.
The s-passive is especially common when describing a general procedure, repeated practice, rule, or established process.

en.value: Applications are registered automatically.
The drawings are assessed by the technical department.
The decision is sent digitally.

spans.value: These sentences describe how the system normally works. They do not direct attention to one particular moment of action.
The bli-passive uses a form of bli followed by a past participle (perfektum partisipp):

en.value: The application is being checked now.
The attachment will be registered tomorrow.
The case will be decided next week.

spans.value: Here the speaker presents the action more clearly as an event affecting a particular application, attachment, or case.
Compare the framing:

no.value: Alle vedlegg kontrolleres før saken behandles.

en.value: All attachments are checked before the case is processed.

no.value: Vedlegget ditt blir kontrollert av Eirik nå.

en.value: Your attachment is being checked by Eirik now.

spans.value: The first sentence gives a general procedure. The second reports a particular event in progress.
The distinction is useful, but it is not absolute. Formal Norwegian often uses an s-passive for a current process as well:

en.value: The case is being processed now.

spans.value: This is natural in status messages, official reports, and administrative language. In ordinary conversation, blir behandlet can make the unfolding event more explicit:

en.value: The case is being processed now.

spans.value: A compact working tendency is:

The present s-passive is common for routines, rules, procedures, and concise formal descriptions. Blir plus the past participle often foregrounds a particular event or what is happening to a particular subject. Context and style can make either construction natural in some cases.
For many verbs ending in unstressed -e, the s-passive is formed by replacing final -e with -es:

en.value: to process → is/are processed
to check → is/are checked
to register → is/are registered
to send → is/are sent

spans.value: For an infinitive without final -e, -s is normally added:

en.value: to receive → is/are received

spans.value: The present bli-passive uses blir plus the past participle:

en.value: The application is being processed.
The attachment is being sent.

no.value: Meldingen blir mottatt av riktig avdeling.

en.value: The message is received by the correct department.

spans.value: Do not combine the two passive markers.
Incorrect:

en.value: 'Incorrect: The application is being processed.'

spans.value: Correct:

en.value: The application is being processed.

spans.value: After blir, use the past participle behandlet, not the s-passive behandles.
Modal verbs such as må, skal, kan, bør, and må not take a present-tense verb after them. They are followed by an infinitive. In passive constructions, the s-passive infinitive is extremely common.

no.value: Vedlegget må sendes inn i dag.

en.value: The attachment must be submitted today.

no.value: Søknaden skal behandles innen tre uker.

en.value: The application is to be processed within three weeks.
The error can be corrected digitally.
Personal information should be removed from the drawing.

spans.value: These constructions are concise and natural for requirements, possibilities, recommendations, and scheduled procedures.
A modal verb can also be followed by bli plus a past participle:

en.value: The application may be rejected.

no.value: Saken skal bli avgjort neste uke.

en.value: The case will be decided next week.

no.value: Vedlegget må bli registrert før fredag.

en.value: The attachment must be registered before Friday.

spans.value: The construction with bli often gives more weight to the event or resulting change. This can matter when the speaker is making a prediction, emphasizing an outcome, or assuring someone that a particular event will occur.
Compare:

no.value: Alle søknader skal behandles innen tre uker.

en.value: All applications are to be processed within three weeks.

no.value: Søknaden din skal bli behandlet innen tre uker.

en.value: Your application will be processed within three weeks.

spans.value: The first fits a general service rule, while the second fits a promise or prediction about one application. Because the subjects also differ, this pair illustrates common contexts rather than isolating the effect of the passive construction.
Another useful contrast is:

en.value: The information can be changed on the website.
The information may be changed later.

spans.value: In the first sentence, kan expresses practical possibility: the website allows the change. In the second, the later time reference supports uncertainty about a future event. Because the complements differ, this pair also does not isolate the passive construction.
To hold the other wording constant, compare:

no.value: Søknaden din kan behandles i morgen.

en.value: Your application can be processed tomorrow.

no.value: Søknaden din kan bli behandlet i morgen.

en.value: Your application may be processed tomorrow.

spans.value: Both are natural. The modal s-passive is concise and can sound neutral or procedural; modal plus bli can foreground the possible occurrence more explicitly. This is a viewpoint tendency, not a categorical difference.
After a modal, Norwegian uses an infinitive rather than a present-tense verb. In this sentence, sendes is the passive infinitive:
Correct:

en.value: The attachment must be submitted.

spans.value: The passive infinitive sendes has the same spelling as the present s-passive used in other contexts, but its function after må is infinitive. Do not add bli merely because English uses be. If bli is used after a modal, it must also be infinitive: må bli, not må blir.

Modal plus s-passive is often concise for a rule, obligation, possibility, or procedure. Modal plus bli plus the participle can foreground a particular event or outcome. These are tendencies, and both constructions may be natural for the same event with a modest difference in framing.

sections.title: Past time: use ble plus the past participle

spans.value: For a completed or ongoing passive event in the past, modern Bokmål normally uses the past tense (preteritum) of bli: ble.

no.value: Søknaden ble mottatt for åtte dager siden.

en.value: The application was received eight days ago.
The attachment was registered this morning.

no.value: Tegningene ble kontrollert av teknisk avdeling.

en.value: The drawings were checked by the technical department.

no.value: Saken ble ikke avgjort på møtet.

en.value: The case was not decided at the meeting.

spans.value: The time expression often makes the past reference clear, but ble itself carries the past tense.
Compare present and past:

en.value: The application is being checked now.
The application was checked yesterday.

spans.value: Do not use blir for a finished event simply because English uses a form of be.
Incorrect:

en.value: 'Incorrect: The application was checked yesterday.'

spans.value: Correct:

en.value: The application was checked yesterday.

spans.value: Past s-passive forms can occur in older, literary, or highly formal language, but they are not the productive everyday choice you need here. For ordinary modern Bokmål, use ble plus the past participle to report a past passive event.
Eirik does this when he checks Maya’s timeline:

en.value: The application was received on Monday.

no.value: Den ble fordelt til en saksbehandler på onsdag.

en.value: It was assigned to a case officer on Wednesday.
The drawings were assessed on Friday.

spans.value: The sequence is clear because each passive event is anchored at a past time.

sections.title: Perfect contexts: har blitt plus the past participle

spans.value: The present perfect (presens perfektum) connects a past event with the present. The present-perfect bli-passive practiced here uses har blitt plus the past participle.

en.value: The attachment has been registered.
The application has been checked.

no.value: Saken har ikke blitt avgjort ennå.

en.value: The case has not been decided yet.
The deadline has been changed.

spans.value: This construction is useful when the current result matters or when the exact past time is not the main point.
Compare the past and the present perfect:

en.value: The attachment was registered at nine o’clock.

no.value: Vedlegget har blitt registrert, så saken kan behandles videre.

en.value: The attachment has been registered, so the case can be processed further.

spans.value: The first sentence locates the event at a finished past time. The second emphasizes its present relevance: the registration is now complete, and the process can continue.
Within this pattern, the three parts retain this relative order:
har + blitt + past participle

en.value: The application has been approved.

spans.value: A common mistake is to omit blitt.
Incorrect:

en.value: 'Not: The application has approved. (for the intended passive meaning)'

spans.value: This changes the grammar and suggests that the application itself has approved something.
Correct:

en.value: The application has been approved.

spans.value: Another mistake is to use an s-passive after har.
Incorrect:

en.value: 'Incorrect: The application has been processed.'

spans.value: Correct:

en.value: The application has been processed.

spans.value: In the perfect passive, blitt carries the passive construction and behandlet is the past participle.
The next morning, Maya checks the portal again and calls Eirik.
Nå står det at vedlegget har blitt registrert.

blocks.translation: Now it says that the attachment has been registered.

spans.value: Flott. Da kan saken behandles videre.

blocks.translation: Great. Then the case can be processed further.

spans.value: Betyr det at tegningene blir vurdert i dag?

blocks.translation: Does that mean the drawings are being assessed today?

spans.value: Ja. De fleste tegninger vurderes automatisk først, men dine blir også kontrollert av en arkitekt.

blocks.translation: Yes. Most drawings are assessed automatically first, but yours are also being checked by an architect.

spans.value: Hva skjer når kontrollen er ferdig?

blocks.translation: What happens when the check is finished?

spans.value: Da blir det skrevet en anbefaling. Saken skal avgjøres på møtet på tirsdag.

blocks.translation: Then a recommendation is written. The case is to be decided at the meeting on Tuesday.

spans.value: Og etter møtet?

blocks.translation: And after the meeting?

spans.value: Når saken har blitt avgjort, blir vedtaket sendt til deg med en gang.

blocks.translation: Once the case has been decided, the decision will be sent to you immediately.

spans.value: Notice how the forms work together:

en.value: Most drawings are assessed automatically.

spans.value: This presents a routine.

no.value: Dine blir også kontrollert av en arkitekt.

en.value: Yours are also being checked by an architect.

spans.value: This concerns a particular set of drawings and a particular event.

en.value: The case is to be decided at the meeting.

spans.value: The modal s-passive presents the scheduled procedure concisely.

no.value: Når saken har blitt avgjort, blir vedtaket sendt.

en.value: Once the case has been decided, the decision will be sent.

spans.value: The first clause looks back from a future point to a completed passive event. The second presents the next event in the process. The chapter’s target remains the passive forms: the time relationship merely gives them a realistic context.
When you need a passive sentence, ask three questions.
First, is the sentence a general rule, routine, or concise procedural description in present time? An s-passive is often the natural choice.

en.value: The documents are stored digitally.

spans.value: Second, does a modal express a requirement, possibility, recommendation, or scheduled procedure? A modal plus s-passive is normally concise and idiomatic.

en.value: The documents must be stored securely.

spans.value: Third, are you presenting a particular passive event in the present, past, or perfect? The bli-passive lets you mark these time perspectives with the appropriate form of bli plus the past participle.

en.value: The document is being checked now.
The document was checked yesterday.
The document has been checked.

spans.value: In present-time formal or administrative language, an s-passive may also describe a particular current event naturally.

Do not treat s-passive and bli-passive as mechanically interchangeable in every sentence. They often describe similar real-world actions, but they can organize the message differently. At B2 level, good control means choosing a form that fits both the time reference and the speaker’s viewpoint.

Now move away from the municipal office. Jonas has left his bicycle at a repair shop. The shop has standard procedures, some repairs are happening now, others happened yesterday, and several stages have already been completed.

Without returning to the explanations, give four brief passive updates about a new service situation: one general present procedure using an s-passive, one requirement using a modal plus s-passive, one event at a specified past time using ble plus the participle, and one completed event with a present result using har blitt plus the participle. These named constructions are required because this is form retrieval, not a claim that context alone always determines one natural passive.

prompt.value: Build two linked status updates. First describe the municipality's general procedure for checking all attachments; then report the particular event involving Maya's attachment now. Use a natural present passive for each framing. The key shows one natural answer; equivalent natural Bokmål present passives are accepted when they preserve both framings.

explanation.value: An s-passive fits a standing routine such as kontrolleres; blir kontrollert naturally presents the specific ongoing event.

prompt.value: Build two linked online status messages. Say that the application is processed automatically with a present s-passive, and that the attachment is being registered now with bli plus the past participle. Do not combine the two passive markers.

explanation.value: Use either the s-passive behandles or blir plus the participle registrert; do not attach -s to a verb after blir.

prompt.value: Build one connected update from three instructions: the attachment must be submitted; the application is to be processed within three weeks; and the information can be changed on the website. Use a passive infinitive directly after each supplied modal.

explanation.value: Place the passive infinitive directly after må, skal, or kan: må sendes, skal behandles, kan endres.

prompt.value: Build two linked statements with the same modal meaning. First state the municipality's general service rule; then give a specific prediction about Maya's application. Use natural modal passives that support both framings. The key shows one defensible answer; equivalent natural choices of modal s-passive or modal plus bli are accepted when they preserve meaning.

explanation.value: A modal plus s-passive states the service rule; modal plus bli and a participle can foreground what will happen to this application.

prompt.value: Build one connected dated timeline from four notes: the application was received on Monday; the attachment was registered this morning; the drawings were checked by the technical department; and the case was decided at the meeting. Use the past-tense form of the passive auxiliary plus the correct past participle in every clause.

explanation.value: Use ble plus the past participle for a completed passive event at a stated past time.

prompt.value: Complete both paired reports: describe the current passive event with blir and the past passive event with ble. The choice between a present s-passive and a present bli-passive is not scored in this activity.

spans.value: Nå
søknaden kontrollert, men i går
søknaden kontrollert.

prompt.value: Build one portal update that reports two completed stages and their present consequence: the application has been checked, the attachment has been registered, so the case can proceed. Use the present-perfect passive pattern and the correct past participle for both completed stages.

explanation.value: Use har blitt plus the past participle for a completed passive event with a present result.

prompt.value: Complete both reports. Use the dated past perspective for the event at nine o'clock and the present-perfect perspective for the completed check whose result matters now. Choose the whole passive auxiliary for each blank.

explanation.value: Use ble with a finished, dated past event; use har blitt when the completed event explains the situation now.

spans.value: Vedlegget
registrert klokka ni. Vedlegget
kontrollert, så saken kan behandles videre.

prompt.value: Build two linked bicycle-shop updates. First describe the shop's routine for checking brakes; then report what is happening to Jonas's bicycle now. Use natural present passives that support the two framings. The key gives one natural answer; equivalent natural Bokmål present passives are accepted when they preserve the framings.

Build one connected set of three repair instructions: the brakes must be replaced; the gears can be adjusted; and the safety check should be completed. Use a suitable modal plus passive infinitive for each meaning. The key shows modal plus s-passive; a natural modal-plus-bli alternative is accepted when it preserves the meaning.

Build two separate bicycle-repair updates in one connected report: state what happened yesterday, then state what has now been completed. Use the past passive for the dated event and the present-perfect passive for the present-relevant stage.

Complete four brief updates in this new service situation. Use the first blank for a general present s-passive, the second for a modal plus s-passive infinitive, the third for ble plus a participle at a specified past time, and the fourth for har blitt plus a participle showing a completed event with a present result. Each blank has one correct option.

spans.value: I det nye kundesenteret
et kundenummer for hver søknad. Vedlegget må
til kundesenteret før fristen. Søknaden
mottatt på mandag. Søknaden
kontrollert; derfor er den klar for videre behandling.
